Reviewer view: the judge's full reasoning

Both of you: this is a route-deviation dispute on trip TRP-02812 (RydeX, metered). The telemetry is clean — 107 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, 10-second sampling, so no POL-RD-07(a)–(c) impairment — and it measures 13.52 km against a booked optimal route of 10.4 km. That is an excess of 3.12 km, or 30.0% of optimal, so both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (above 20% and above 0.8 km) and a deviation is established on this trip's trace alone. The rider's claim that the trace establishes a deviation is accepted, and the trace figure, not the rounded trip-record copy of 13.5 km, governs.

How to appeal: You may appeal once within 30 days (POL-GEN-04). A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 0.00 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

Draft 1 - sampled
Both of you: this is a route-deviation dispute on trip TRP-02812 (RydeX, metered). The telemetry is clean — 107 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, 10-second sampling, so no POL-RD-07(a)–(c) impairment — and it measures 13.52 km against a booked optimal route of 10.4 km. That is an excess of 3.12 km, or 30.0% of optimal, so both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (above 20% and above 0.8 km) and a deviation is established on this trip's trace alone. The rider's claim that the trace establishes a deviation is accepted, and the trace figure, not the rounded trip-record copy of 13.5 km, governs. The driver nonetheless has a complete answer under POL-RD-04. Chat message MSG-02812-001, sent by the rider at 10:19:39 — about a minute after the meter started at 10:18:39 and well before the waypoint was reached at 10:27:39 — reads 'can we stop at Paya Lebar Square first, need to grab something'. It comes from the rider, it is timely, and it names a specific, actionable place. The GPS trace corroborates it: the waypoint resolved from chat_message.waypoint_hint (1.381532, 103.831811) is passed within 35.99 m at fix 54, far inside the 200 m test, so this is not the uncorroborated-instruction case in POL-RD-14 and no POL-RD-10(7) contradiction arises. POL-RD-04 therefore applies, and it excludes the excess distance between the vehicle leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor. On this record that excursion is the whole of the excess. The only off-corridor movement is the single requested waypoint, passed once, with no second waypoint hinted in the chat, no pickup or dropoff amendment on the trip record, and no ERP line in the fare breakdown at all (on-route, off-route and total all 0.00), so there is no other detour the excess could consist of. The requested point sits well off the booked corridor, and the added distance is the natural cost of going there and back. Excluding it leaves no excess meeting POL-RD-01, no deviation survives, and POL-RD-02 — which runs only where a deviation is established — is never reached. I reject the rider's argument that the driver failed to prove the size of the exonerated stretch. POL-RD-04 requires a corroborated rider instruction, not a separate detour-distance artifact; once the instruction is corroborated, the excursion is excluded by operation of the clause, and the driver discharged his POL-RD-08 burden by pointing to a specific artifact (EV-CHAT-02812) and a specific clause (POL-RD-04). The rider's complaint that they asked only for a 'quick stop, not a tour' does not change where the stop was: the place they named is off the booked route. The rest of the record changes nothing. EV-ADVIS-02812-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and can carry no fact; POL-RD-13 is not engaged because the driver relies on no external traffic cause, so nothing turns on the absence of an advisory. No POL-RD-06 conduct referral arises: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 368 completed trips in 90 days, so no pattern is established, and the deviation is not MATERIAL in any event. POL-RD-09 corrects nothing — there are no ERP, toll or surcharge lines, and limb (3) bars an ERP refund where the detour is rider-caused. The rider's serial-claimant corroboration step under POL-RD-08 is not triggered (deviation_claims_60d = 0), and the rider's profile fields are not used against anyone. Result: NO_ACTION. Under POL-GEN-03 this is party-relative — fare_breakdown.payment_status of CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 stand exactly as they are; the rider is not refunded and nothing is taken back from the driver. For completeness, had the deviation survived, POL-RD-02 against the booked optimal would have given charged_total 19.69 less a recomputed_fare of 16.32 = 3.37, rounded up to SGD 3.40; that computation does not run. No clause produces a referral, and the monetary effect of zero is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold, so nothing is held and the ruling executes on issue.
Draft 2 - sampled
To the rider and the driver: the trip's own telemetry shows a real difference, but it is the difference the rider asked for, so nothing is refunded and the SGD 19.69 charge stands. The deviation is established on the numbers. Under POL-RD-01 the governing measurement is the trace figure, not the rounded trip-record copy: EV-GPS-02812 (weight 1.0, unimpaired — 107 fixes, 100.0% coverage, 10 s sampling, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s) measures 13.52 km against the booked optimal of 10.4 km. The excess is 3.12 km, 30.0% of optimal, which passes both establishment tests (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km). The rider therefore discharged the initial POL-RD-08 burden, and trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown (TRP-02812). That excess is then fully exonerated under POL-RD-04. The chat log EV-CHAT-02812 shows the rider writing at 10:19:39, sixty seconds after the meter started at 10:18:39, 'can we stop at Paya Lebar Square first, need to grab something', and the driver answering 'ok'. That is an instruction from the rider, well inside the three-minute window, naming a specific place.
